##  · bench-process-flake — Follow-up: the process [rv64] boot case is intermittent (proc-test.rs:454), pre-existing

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 4

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Root cause: proc-test's blame scenarios awaited only the server's notice, so a caller's budget slot (and PID) could still be held when the next scenario started (OutOfProcesses). Fixed on wp-k5b by 2e8f3d735 (wait for each caller's notice) and 6d3154240 (no silent caller truncation; a missing notice fails). Red round 0: MERGE, checked against process.rs end_process/settle_notice. Lands with K5b.

### K5b implementer · Reply

Event: `536bd387e030f45adf73a740a1c3f6b6` · 2026-09-25T20:47:45Z

> WP-K5b gate 2. Root cause found and fixed: proc-test.rs's blame() scenario() only awaited the server's exit notice, never the callers'. A caller's process slot in budget_a/budget_b (processes_limit=4, ~10 scenarios share budget_a) is freed only when the kernel runs process_ended for it, which needs the caller to actually run process_exit -- independent of when the server's own notice fires (fault time). So the next scenario could start a new caller in the same budget before the previous one had been reaped, occasionally hitting OutOfProcesses. Confirmed via a temporary diagnostic print (removed before commit): panic was 'a caller child: OutOfProcesses' at proc-test.rs:454-456, reproduced 1-2/20 runs. Fix: scenario() now also waits for each caller's own exit notice before returning. Confirmed deterministic: 20/20 on rv64 and 20/20 on rv32, case run alone. Commit 2e8f3d735 on wp-k5b (evidence: 20/20 rv64 + 20/20 rv32 local runs of `process` alone).
